examples.en: I climbed the mountain at the break of dawn.
As dawn broke, the sea turned red.

examples.ko: 동터 오는 하늘을 보면서 소원을 빌었어요.
examples.en: I made a wish while watching the sky brighten with dawn.

examples.ko: 날이 밝기 직전, 동트기 전이 제일 어두워요.
examples.en: Right before the day brightens, just before dawn, is the darkest.
As soon as day broke, the farmers went out to the fields.

examples.ko: 날이 막 동텄을 때 우리는 정상에 도착했어요.
examples.en: We reached the summit just as dawn broke.

explain: 해가 뜨기 전에 먼동이 밝아 오기 시작하는 것을 말해요. 해 자체가 뜨는 '해가 뜨다'와 달라요. 일상 대화에서는 '날이 밝다'를 더 많이 쓰고, '동이 트다'처럼 띄어 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: We talked until dawn broke.
phrases.nuance_ko: '동트다'와 뜻이 같고, 띄어 쓴 이 형태로도 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 동트다; also very commonly said in this spaced form.

phrases.en: I woke up before dawn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해 뜨기 전 시간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For the time before sunrise.

phrases.en: We talked all night and it got light.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 더 많이 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar phrase more common in daily speech.

explain_en: It describes the first light of dawn appearing before the sun rises, which differs from '해가 뜨다' where the sun itself rises. In daily talk '날이 밝다' is more common, and it can also be written as '동이 트다'.

t90.ax: As dawn broke, the sea turned red.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 우승을 목전에 두고 있어요.
examples.en: Our team is right on the verge of winning the championship.

examples.ko: 시험이 목전이라 요즘 잠을 잘 못 자요.
examples.en: The exam is just around the corner, so I haven't been sleeping well lately.
That athlete missed the gold medal at the very last moment.
Success is within reach, so I can't give up.

examples.ko: 목전의 이익만 보고 결정하면 후회할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you decide only by looking at immediate gain, you may regret it.

examples.ko: 경기 종료가 목전이었지만 아직 희망이 있어요.
examples.en: The end of the game is imminent, but there is still hope.

explain: '눈앞'과 비슷한 뜻이고, 시간적으로 곧 닥칠 때 '목전에 두다'로 많이 써요. 말할 때는 '코앞'이라고 편하게 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: The exam is right around the corner, so I'm anxious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 '목전' 대신 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual word people use in speech instead of 목전.

phrases.example: 우리 팀이 우승을 눈앞에 두고 있어요.
phrases.en: Our team is on the verge of winning the championship.
phrases.nuance_ko: '목전에 두다'와 같은 뜻으로 일상에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 목전에 두다 but more common in daily speech.
phrases.en_equiv: to be on the verge of

phrases.en: The deadline is right upon us, so I'm busy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곧 해야 할 일이나 일이 아주 가까이 왔을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is about to happen very soon.

explain_en: Formal; something big is about to happen (시험이 목전에) It is close to '눈앞' (right before one's eyes), and is often used in the fixed phrase '목전에 두다' when something is about to happen. In casual speech people also say '코앞'.

t90.ax: Success is within reach, so I can't give up.

examples.en: Spring is just now beginning.
A new era is just now opening up.
It is now the height of summer vacation season.
The moment we were waiting for has finally arrived.
This city is now in full festival mood.
Now is the time to announce the results.

explain: '이제 막, 지금 한창'이라는 느낌으로 문장 맨 앞에 자주 오는 글 느낌의 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '이제 곧, 드디어'가 더 자연스러워요. 계절이나 시대가 바뀌는 때를 말할 때 어울려요.

phrases.en: It is now truly the age of artificial intelligence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로운 시대가 한창 시작되었다고 말할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits when saying a new era has truly begun.

phrases.en: It is just about time for the flowers to bloom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 막 일어날 때를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Marks the moment something is just about to happen.

phrases.en: Spring is coming very soon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대화에서는 '바야흐로'보다 이 말이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In conversation, this sounds more natural than 바야흐로.

explain_en: Literary; a big change or season about to begin. It feels like 'right now, just at the point of', and often opens a sentence in a written or formal tone. In everyday talk '이제 곧' or '드디어' sounds more natural. It suits moments when a season or era is changing.

examples.en: Now is a period of great change for society.

examples.ko: 조선 말기는 나라 전체가 흔들리던 변혁기였어요.
examples.en: The late Joseon period was an era of upheaval for the whole country.
In times of transformation, new ideas spread fast.

examples.ko: 산업이 변혁기를 맞아 많은 회사가 사업을 바꾸고 있어요.
examples.en: As the industry enters a time of transformation, many companies are changing their business.

examples.ko: 우리 세대는 기술의 변혁기에 살고 있어요.
examples.en: Our generation is living through a technological revolution.
The more things are changing, the more important it is to prepare calmly.

explain: '변혁'은 제도나 사회 구조가 근본적으로 바뀌는 것이라 '변화'보다 훨씬 크고 무거운 느낌이에요. '전환기'와 비슷하게 쓰지만, 변혁기는 더 큰 흔들림을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.example: 우리 사회는 지금 변혁기를 맞고 있어요.
phrases.en: Our society is now facing a period of great change.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 변화의 시기가 왔다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means that a time of major change has arrived.
phrases.en_equiv: to face a period of upheaval

phrases.example: 변혁기의 사회에서는 모든 것이 빠르게 바뀌어요.
phrases.en: In a society in a period of upheaval, everything changes fast.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의'를 붙여 어떤 시기의 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 의 describes what something is like in that period.
phrases.en_equiv: society in a period of upheaval

phrases.en: Now is a turning point when industry is changing greatly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '변혁기'와 비슷하지만 흔들림이 조금 덜한 변화에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 변혁기, but can be used for less dramatic change.

explain_en: '변혁' means a fundamental change in systems or social structure, so it feels much bigger and heavier than '변화'. It is used similarly to '전환기' (turning point), but '변혁기' fits when the shake-up is bigger.

examples.ko: 불볕 아래에서 한 시간 걷고 나니 지쳤어요.
examples.en: After walking for an hour under the scorching sun, I was exhausted.

examples.ko: 불볕더위가 계속돼서 에어컨 없이는 못 살아요.
examples.en: The scorching heat keeps going, so I can't live without an air conditioner.

examples.ko: 한낮의 불볕이 너무 뜨거워서 모자를 썼어요.
examples.en: The midday sun was so hot that I put on a hat.

examples.ko: 불볕에 오래 있으면 열사병에 걸릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you stay long in the burning sun, you can get heatstroke.

examples.ko: 올여름은 불볕더위 때문에 전기 요금이 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: This summer the electricity bill was high because of the scorching heat.

examples.ko: 불볕 같은 햇빛 속에서 농부들이 일하고 있어요.
examples.en: Farmers are working in sunlight as fierce as a blaze.

explain: '불볕더위'처럼 쓰는 경우가 가장 흔해요. 뉴스나 일기예보에서는 비슷한 말로 '폭염'도 써요. 햇볕이 불처럼 뜨겁게 내리쬐는 느낌을 살려 주는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 불볕더위 때문에 낮에는 밖에 나가기 힘들어요.
phrases.en: Because of the scorching heat, it's hard to go out during the day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불볕'이 가장 흔하게 쓰이는 말로, 몹시 심한 여름 더위를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use of '불볕', meaning extremely intense summer heat.

phrases.en: The sun beats down at noon, so I long for shade.
phrases.nuance_ko: 햇볕이 아주 뜨겁게 비치는 모습을 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paints the picture of the sun shining down fiercely.

phrases.en: It's an extreme heat wave today, so drink lots of water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷한 말로, 뉴스나 일기예보에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word, used more in news and weather reports.

explain_en: It is most common in the compound '불볕더위' (scorching heat). In news and weather forecasts, '폭염' is also used as a similar word. It conveys the sense of sunlight beating down as hot as fire.

t90.ax: The midday sun was so hot that I put on a hat.

en: a place bright as day at night; a city that never sleeps

examples.ko: 연휴라서 시내 거리가 밤새 불야성을 이뤘어요.
examples.en: Because of the holiday, the downtown streets were lit up and busy all night.
On Christmas Eve, Myeongdong is bright and bustling all night.

examples.ko: 축제 기간에는 이 동네가 불야성이 돼요.
examples.en: During the festival, this neighborhood stays lit and lively all night.

examples.ko: 불야성 같은 도시의 밤 풍경이 정말 예뻐요.
examples.en: The night view of the city, bright as day, is really pretty.
The night market stays bright and crowded until dawn.

examples.ko: 밤마다 불야성인 거리라서 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: The street is bright and noisy every night, so I can't sleep.

explain: 밤에도 불빛이 환하고 사람이 많은 곳을 '불야성을 이루다', '불야성이다'로 말해요. 주로 번화가, 시장, 축제 거리에 써요. 신문이나 글에서 더 자주 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '밤새 환하다'처럼 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: Tourists took in the street that never sleeps.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의'로 이어서 밤에도 환한 거리나 도시를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Linked with '의' to describe a street or city that stays bright at night.

phrases.en: During the festival, downtown is lit up and busy all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밤에도 불빛이 환하고 사람이 많은 모습을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for a place that is bright and crowded at night.
phrases.en_equiv: to be lit up all night

phrases.en: During the festival, downtown stays bright all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '불야성' 대신 이렇게 쉽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily talk, this is the easier way to say it.

explain_en: It describes a place that stays brightly lit and crowded at night, as in '불야성을 이루다' or '불야성이다'. It is used for busy downtown areas, markets and festival streets. It shows up more in newspapers and writing, while daily talk may say '밤새 환하다'.

examples.en: I got up at the first light of dawn and climbed the mountain.
The air at early dawn is very cold and clear.
My father went out to work from the break of dawn.
The streets at early dawn are very quiet.
A call came at the crack of dawn and I was startled.
I studied for the exam until the first light of dawn.

explain: 날이 막 밝아 오기 시작하는 이른 시각을 말해요. 그냥 '새벽'보다 글이나 이야기 속에서 분위기 있게 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I left for the airport in the early dawn.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신새벽'과 뜻이 비슷하고 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 신새벽 and more casual in daily talk.

phrases.en: The streets at first light are very quiet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의'를 붙이면 분위기 있는 글에서 장면을 그릴 때 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '의' it sets a scene nicely in descriptive writing.

phrases.en: The rain stopped around daybreak.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날이 밝아 올 무렵을 말하는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word for the time when day is about to break.

explain_en: It names the very early moment when daylight is just beginning to appear. It is a more atmospheric word than plain '새벽' and is common in writing and storytelling.

examples.en: I went out for a walk as dusk fell.

examples.ko: 새벽 어스름 속에서 첫 버스가 왔어요.
examples.en: The first bus came in the dim light of dawn.
At twilight, the lights came on in house after house.

examples.ko: 저녁 어스름에 길이 잘 안 보여서 조심했어요.
examples.en: The road was hard to see in the evening dusk, so I was careful.
Someone was walking toward me in the half-light.
The train came in through the dim light.

explain: 해 질 무렵뿐 아니라 동트기 전에도 써서 '저녁 어스름', '새벽 어스름'처럼 말해요. '땅거미'는 저녁에만 쓴다는 점이 달라요.

phrases.en: The market grew quiet in the evening dusk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해 질 무렵의 어둑한 때를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the dim time around sunset.

phrases.en: Dusk began to settle over the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어둑한 기운이 퍼지는 모습을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common way to describe the dim light spreading.

phrases.en: I came home at dusk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에'를 붙여 그 시간대를 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding the particle 에 marks that time of day.

explain_en: It can be used both at sunset and before sunrise, as in '저녁 어스름' and '새벽 어스름'. '땅거미' differs in that it is used for the evening only.

examples.ko: 동쪽 하늘에 여명이 밝아 오기 시작했어요.
examples.en: Dawn began to light up the eastern sky.

examples.ko: 새벽 여명 속에서 산길을 천천히 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked slowly along the mountain path in the dawn light.
We set out around daybreak.

examples.ko: 이 발명은 새로운 시대의 여명을 알렸어요.
examples.en: This invention heralded the dawn of a new era.
I took a photo of the sky tinted by the dawn.
The city slowly wakes up in the first light.

explain: 날이 막 밝아 올 때의 희미한 빛이에요. 일상에서는 '새벽'이라고 하고, 여명은 글이나 노래, 비유 표현에서 더 자주 보여요. '새 시대의 여명'처럼 무언가가 시작되는 때를 비유하기도 해요. 같은 소리로 '남은 목숨'을 뜻하는 여명(餘命)도 있어요.

phrases.en: I woke up at dawn and took a walk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '여명' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy word used in daily life instead of 여명.

phrases.en: That invention was the dawn of a new era.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무언가 새롭게 시작되는 때를 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative phrase for the beginning of something new.
phrases.en_equiv: the dawn of a new era

phrases.example: 창문 너머로 여명이 밝아 오기 시작했어요.
phrases.en: The first light of dawn began to brighten beyond the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날이 막 밝아 올 때의 희미한 빛을 표현하며, 글이나 노래에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the faint light as day begins to break, often used in writing and songs.

explain_en: Literary; first light of day, or the beginning of a new era. It is the faint light just as the day begins to break. In daily life people say '새벽', while '여명' shows up more in writing, songs and figurative expressions. It can also describe the beginning of something, as in '새 시대의 여명'. A different word with the same sound, 여명(餘命), means the remaining life of a person.

examples.en: That actor has a sophisticated, city-like image.
This cafe has an urbane, stylish atmosphere.
Her outfit is urbane, so it stands out.
Even though he is from the countryside, his way of speaking is urbane.
The room decorated in an urbane style is very neat.
It is a design that stands out for its urbane sense.

explain: 사람, 옷차림, 분위기가 세련되고 도시 사람 같을 때 칭찬하는 느낌으로 써요. '도시적'과 비슷하지만 도회적은 세련된 이미지가 더 강해요. 반대 느낌은 '소박하다', '시골스럽다'예요.

phrases.en: This outfit has an urbane feel.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도회적'은 '-인' 꼴로 명사를 꾸밀 때 가장 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: '도회적' is most natural in the '-인' form before a noun.

phrases.en: My older sister has a sophisticated, city-like look.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서술어로 쓰면 사람이 세련되어 보인다는 칭찬이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a predicate, it praises someone for looking sophisticated.

phrases.en: It's a building with an urban design.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도회적'과 비슷하지만 세련됨보다 도시다운 모습에 초점이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but focuses more on looking like a city than on sophistication.

explain_en: It is used with a complimentary feel for a person, outfit or atmosphere that looks refined and like a city dweller. It is close to '도시적', but 도회적 has a stronger image of sophistication. The opposite feeling is '소박하다' or '시골스럽다'.

examples.en: The books are lined up neatly on the bookshelf.
The child's handwriting is neat and straight, so it's easy to read.
I walked along the straight, orderly road.
The desks in the classroom look lined up in neat rows.
I feel good when the inside of the closet is neatly arranged.
It is a village known for its neatly squared fields.

explain: 여러 개가 모두 곧고 바르게 정돈된 모습에 써요. '반듯하다'는 하나의 물건이나 사람의 행실이 바를 때도 쓰지만, '반듯반듯하다'는 여러 개가 줄지어 있을 때 잘 어울려요. 반의어는 '삐뚤빼뚤하다'예요.

phrases.en: I stacked the documents neatly and straight.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙여 여러 개를 가지런히 두는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-게', it describes arranging many items neatly in order.

phrases.en: I wrote the letter in neat, straight handwriting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글자 여러 개가 가지런할 때 잘 어울리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A good pairing when many letters are written evenly.

phrases.en: The line wasn't straight, so we lined up again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 정돈이 안 된 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, describing something that isn't tidy or aligned.

explain_en: It describes many things that are all straight and neatly arranged. '반듯하다' can also be used for a single object or a person's proper behavior, but '반듯반듯하다' fits best when many things are lined up. The opposite is '삐뚤빼뚤하다' (crooked).

en: to be noisy; to be flashy; to be making a fuss

examples.en: The kids are running around noisily, so it's loud.
I woke up startled by the loud racket.

examples.ko: 결혼식을 너무 요란스럽지 않게 하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to have a wedding that isn't too flashy.

examples.ko: 왜 이렇게 요란스러워요? 조금만 조용히 해 주세요.
examples.en: Why are you making such a fuss? Please be a bit quieter.
The outfit was so loud that everyone stared.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 개업 행사를 요란스럽게 했어요.
examples.en: That shop held a lavish, noisy opening event.

explain: 소리가 시끄러울 때뿐 아니라 옷차림, 행사, 색깔이 지나치게 화려하고 눈에 띌 때도 써요. '요란하다'와 쓰임이 가까워요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '요란스러워요', '요란스러운'으로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: The street is so noisy and flashy today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체 활용형으로, ㅂ이 '워'로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The 해요체 form, where ㅂ changes to 워.

phrases.en: I stood out because of my flashy outfit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷이 지나치게 화려할 때 명사를 꾸미는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for clothes that are overly flashy.

phrases.en: We kept the wedding small and not showy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조용하고 소박하다는 뜻으로 부정형을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form means quiet and modest.

explain_en: It is used not only for loud noise but also for outfits, events or colors that are overly flashy and attention-grabbing. Its usage is close to '요란하다'. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '요란스러워요' and '요란스러운'.

t90.ax: I woke up startled by the loud racket.

examples.ko: 나무 밑에 개미가 우글우글 모여 있어요.
examples.en: Ants are gathered in swarms under the tree.

examples.ko: 휴가철 공항에 사람들이 우글우글 몰려 있어요.
examples.en: People are crowded together at the airport in the holiday season.
The fish in the tank are swarming around.

examples.ko: 쓰레기통 주변에 벌레가 우글우글 있어서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled because bugs were swarming around the trash can.
Kids gathered in crowds at the amusement park.

examples.ko: 우글우글 모여 있는 비둘기를 피해서 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked around the pigeons flocked together.

explain: '우글우글 + 모이다/몰리다/있다'처럼 쓰고, 우글거리는 모양을 나타내요. 사람이 많을 때는 '바글바글'도 비슷하게 자주 말해요. 벌레나 동물이 모여 있는 모습에도 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: The weekend market is packed with people.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우글우글'과 비슷하지만 사람이 많은 곳에 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but used more often for crowds of people.

phrases.en: Customers crowd in on the first day of the sale.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한꺼번에 많이 모여드는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes many coming together all at once.

phrases.example: 풀밭에 작은 벌레가 우글우글 기어 다녀요.
phrases.en: Small bugs crawl around in swarms on the grass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌레나 동물이 많이 움직이는 모습에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits insects or animals moving in large numbers.

explain_en: It is used like '우글우글 + 모이다/몰리다/있다' to show the swarming look. For lots of people, '바글바글' is also often used in a similar way. It suits scenes of bugs or animals huddled together.

en: galaxy of stars; array of luminaries

examples.ko: 그 대회에는 기라성 같은 선수들이 나왔어요.
examples.en: A galaxy of star players took part in that tournament.

examples.ko: 기라성 같은 선배들 사이에서 발표하려니 떨렸어요.
examples.en: I was nervous presenting among such a star-studded group of seniors.

examples.ko: 이 학교에서는 기라성 같은 작가들이 나왔어요.
examples.en: A host of famous writers came out of this school.

examples.ko: 기라성 같은 인물들 중에서도 그분이 제일 유명해요.
examples.en: Even among such stars, that person is the most famous.

examples.ko: 영화에는 기라성 같은 배우들이 줄줄이 나와요.
examples.en: One famous actor after another appears in the film.

examples.ko: 기라성 같은 대학 동기들이 지금은 각 분야에서 활약해요.
examples.en: My star-studded college classmates are now active in their own fields.

explain: 거의 '기라성 같은'의 꼴로 쓰고, 뛰어난 사람이 여럿 모여 있을 때 말해요. 사람 한 명보다는 여러 명을 가리킬 때 자연스러워요. 주로 글이나 방송에서 보여요.

phrases.en: A galaxy of stars gathered at the award ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유명한 사람이 여럿 모였을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when many famous people are gathered.

phrases.en: History has many outstanding figures.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뛰어난 사람이 많다는 칭찬의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Praises the large number of outstanding people.

explain_en: It is almost always used in the form '기라성 같은', when many outstanding people are gathered. It sounds natural for a group rather than a single person. You mostly see it in writing and broadcasts.
